questions.q: How are the logical states of the 3-qubit phase-flip code defined?
questions.explain: The phase-flip code encodes in the Hadamard (X) basis: |0>_L = |+++> and |1>_L = |--->, the rotated analogue of the bit-flip code's |000>/|111>.

questions.q: What are the stabilizer generators of the 3-qubit phase-flip code?
options: Z1Z2 and Z2Z3
Y1Y2 and Y2Y3
X1Z2 and Z2X3
X1X2 and X2X3
questions.explain: The phase-flip code's stabilizers are X1X2 and X2X3 -- the Hadamard-basis analogue of the bit-flip code's Z1Z2 and Z2Z3.

questions.q: Why does a Z error on one qubit of this code behave exactly like an X error does on the bit-flip code?
options: Because the phase-flip code secretly uses the computational basis, not the Hadamard basis
This is a coincidence with no underlying reason
Z errors and X errors are mathematically identical operators
A Z error swaps |+> and |-> exactly the way an X error swaps |0> and |1>, so the same syndrome logic applies in the rotated basis
questions.explain: The X/Z basis duality means Z acts on |+>,|-> the same way X acts on |0>,|1>, which is exactly why the phase-flip code's construction and syndrome table mirror the bit-flip code's.

questions.q: According to the verified syndrome table, what does a syndrome of (X1X2, X2X3) = (0,1) indicate?
options: A Z error occurred on qubit 1
A Z error occurred on qubit 3 -- apply Z to qubit 3 to correct
No error occurred
An X error occurred on qubit 2
questions.explain: The verified table shows errorPos=2 (qubit 3) gives syndrome 01, uniquely identifying qubit 3 as needing a corrective Z application.

questions.q: Why can't the phase-flip code detect an X (bit-flip) error on one of its qubits?
options: X errors are physically impossible once a qubit is encoded this way
X errors always produce the same syndrome as a Z error on qubit 2
The phase-flip code actually does detect X errors using the same table
X1X2 and X2X3 commute with X errors, so an X error leaves both stabilizer outcomes unchanged, giving a syndrome of 00 even though the state was corrupted
questions.explain: Just as the bit-flip code was blind to Z errors, the phase-flip code is blind to X errors for the mirrored reason -- its stabilizers don't anticommute with X, so no disagreement is detected.
